Use students' own essays and myths from the unit."},{"type":"text-reference","title":"The Lightning Thief and student essay drafts","pages":"Student's chosen myth passages and own essay"},{"type":"paragraph","audience":"shared","text":"**Reteach.** A thesis names the shared lesson across myths. A thesis can use *although*, *while*, or *because* to show a comparison."},{"type":"teacher-script","move":"say","text":"Let's find the missing piece of your essay. Put your finger on your thesis, then on your strongest evidence. Do they match?"},{"type":"teacher-script","move":"ask","text":"What shared lesson does your thesis say the myths teach?"},{"type":"sample-response","text":"My thesis says that both Greek and Egyptian myths teach that pride leads to downfall."},{"type":"teacher-script","move":"ask","text":"Which detail from a myth best proves that, and how does it prove it?"},{"type":"sample-response","text":"Arachne bragged she was better than Athena and was turned into a spider. This shows that pride brought a punishment, which supports my thesis."},{"type":"teacher-script","move":"say","text":"Quick Check: write one sentence of evidence and one sentence of explanation for the paragraph you still need. Use: In the myth of ___, ___. This shows that ___."},{"type":"eld-panel","purpose":"Help English learners connect a myth detail to a thesis in complete sentences.","sayAsk":"Say: Point to the detail. Then say it with me. Frames: The shared lesson is ___. In the myth of ___, ___. This shows that ___. Ask: Which words tell what happened in the myth?","watchFor":"If a student retells the whole myth, then prompt: Which one detail proves your thesis? If a student states a detail without explaining, then prompt: Finish: This shows that... Success: student gives a specific detail and an explanation sentence."},{"type":"support-table","rows":[{"situation":"Struggling with: connecting evidence to the thesis","tryThis":"Give the frame In the myth of ___, ___. Keep tense consistent: present tense when explaining what a myth shows."},{"type":"teacher-script","move":"say","text":"Read one body paragraph aloud and listen for sentences that sound like talking to a friend or that jump between past and present."},{"type":"teacher-script","move":"ask","text":"Which word or phrase sounds too casual, and what could replace it?"},{"type":"sample-response","text":"I wrote that Zeus is super mad. I could change it to Zeus is furious, which sounds more formal and precise."},{"type":"teacher-script","move":"ask","text":"Where could a transition help your reader see how two myths connect?"},{"type":"sample-response","text":"Between my Greek paragraph and my Norse paragraph, I could add In contrast, or Similarly, to show how they compare."},{"type":"teacher-script","move":"say","text":"Quick Check: revise one sentence to be formal, in present tense, and add one transition."},{"type":"eld-panel","purpose":"Support English learners in choosing precise formal words and comparison transitions.","sayAsk":"Say: In conversation we say ___; in an essay we say ___. Frames: A more formal way to say that is ___. Similarly, ___. In contrast, ___. Ask: Are these two ideas alike or different?","watchFor":"If a student changes one word but the sentence stays casual, then prompt: Reread the whole sentence. Does it all sound formal? If a student picks the wrong transition, then prompt: Are the ideas alike or different? Success: student uses a fitting transition and formal wording."},{"type":"support-table","rows":[{"situation":"Struggling with: finding casual language","tryThis":"Offer a short swap list: super → very or extremely, kinda → somewhat, a lot of → many, mad → furious."},{"situation":"Ready for extension","tryThis":"Have students combine two sentences with an appositive or an *although* clause while keeping the style formal."}]}]},{"id":"huddle-3-present-modern-values","title":"Huddle 3: Presenting a Claim, Evidence, and Modern-Value Connection","minutes":13,"standards":[],"routine":"Huddle","blocks":[{"type":"paragraph","audience":"teacher","text":"Pull students who have not yet presented, or who need to rehearse for the seminar or podcast (Lessons 40, 41). Paraphrase what a partner says before you respond. Speak formally and clearly."},{"type":"teacher-script","move":"say","text":"Say your claim, evidence, and modern value in about one minute. Your partner will paraphrase it back to you."},{"type":"teacher-script","move":"ask","text":"What modern value connects to the lesson in your myths?"},{"type":"sample-response","text":"Humility connects. Today people still admire those who stay modest, just like the myths warn against pride."},{"type":"teacher-script","move":"ask","text":"How can you paraphrase your partner's claim?"},{"type":"sample-response","text":"You said that myths from different cultures teach that pride is dangerous, and you gave the Arachne story as proof."},{"type":"teacher-script","move":"say","text":"Quick Check: present your three parts once while your partner checks that each one is there."},{"type":"teacher-note","variant":"note","text":"If any student still has not presented, record or hear them during this Huddle or while others work independently. Keep it low pressure."},{"type":"eld-panel","purpose":"Give English learners sentence frames to speak formally and paraphrase a partner.","sayAsk":"Say: Practice with a partner first. Frames: My claim is ___. My strongest evidence is ___. This connects to the modern value of ___. So you are saying that ___. Ask: What is your strongest evidence?","watchFor":"If a student reads the essay word for word, then prompt: Say it in your own words using your three frames. If a student skips the modern value, then prompt: What do people still care about today? Success: student states all three parts and paraphrases a partner."},{"type":"support-table","rows":[{"situation":"Struggling with: speaking without reading","tryThis":"Have the student write the claim, evidence, and value on three note cards and practice with a partner before presenting."},{"situation":"Ready for extension","tryThis":"Have students add a response to a partner's claim that connects both students' myths and modern values, using a paraphrase first."}]}]}]},{"kind":"look-back","title":"Look Back","purpose":"Students reflect on progress and set a next step before the unit review.","activities":[{"id":"look-back-quick-write","title":"Quick Write: Where I Am Now","minutes":5,"standards":[],"routine":"Quick Write","blocks":[{"type":"directions","text":"Write 2-3 sentences. I still want to review how transitions show comparison."},{"type":"teacher-note","variant":"note","text":"Invite 2-3 students to share.
